test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How many major banks were nationalised by the government in 1969?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• It was on **July 19, 1969, **when then prime minister Indira Gandhi** **declared the** nationalisation of ******14****** commercial Indian banks **with deposits of over Rs 50 crores.
 
• In 1969,** Allahabad Bank, Canara Bank, United Bank of India, UCO Bank, Syndicate Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Maharashtra, Central Bank of India, Indian Bank, Dena Bank, Union Bank and were nationalised.**
 
• The government of India issued the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1969, and nationalized the **14 largest commercial banks** with effect from **midnight of 19 July 1969.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​**The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is **India's central banking and monetary authority**.
 
• **Canara Bank** is the **third largest **nationalised bank in India.** **
 
• **Dena Bank** was a** government-owned bank **that in 2019 integrated with the **Bank of Baroda. **
 
• **Union Bank of India**, generally mention as** Union Bank or UBI** is an Indian government-owned bank with **120+ million customers.**
